title: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance
subtitle: A Belmont searches for a missing friend
summary: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is Konami's second Game Boy Advance exploration adventure in the series. Juste Belmont, Simon's grandson, enters a mysterious castle while searching for his kidnapped childhood friend. His whip supplies the familiar starting point, while experience, equipment and magic develop his options as the journey continues. body: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is Konami's second Game Boy Advance exploration adventure in the series. Juste Belmont, Simon's grandson, enters a mysterious castle while searching for his kidnapped childhood friend. His whip supplies the familiar starting point, while experience, equipment and magic develop his options as the journey continues. The castle's interconnected routes make movement abilities and remembered obstacles central to progress. What initially appears to be a single building becomes a more complicated place to understand, requiring attention to the relationship between its different versions as well as its individual rooms.

Juste's magical options combine spell books with the subweapons found during exploration. The result depends on the pairing, allowing a familiar item to behave differently when another book is selected. This makes the growing collection useful through combinations rather than simply replacing an earlier attack with a stronger one. Whip combat remains available alongside those effects, giving the player several ways to approach a difficult enemy. Finding another magical component can therefore change the practical value of something already carried and invite another experiment before the next encounter begins.

Progress involves traversing two forms of the castle, with their maps creating related spaces that must be understood together. An ability or discovery in one part of the journey can open another route through the larger structure. Equipment and character growth support the same exploration, helping Juste survive the enemies guarding what remains unknown. Harmony of Dissonance uses the doubled setting to give the map a further layer of uncertainty, asking the player to recognise a place while still considering what may be different about its present form and available connections.
